title: Geometric stalk comparison for a coefficient dual
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative noetherian ring, and $F$ a finite locally constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant]. For every geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $\Omega$ a separably closed field, there is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules $(\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(F,\Lambda_X))_s\cong\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(F_s,\Lambda)$.

source.place: IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf.ihom_unit docstring, local finite presentation and dual finite generation

proof.text: Fix s and an étale trivializing neighborhood through which s lifts. On this neighborhood F is constant with value M, identified with F_s, and M is finitely generated. Noetherianity gives a finite presentation Λᵐ → Λⁿ → M → 0. After exact constant sheafification, internal Hom into the unit is the kernel of the transposed finite matrix. The geometric stalk functor is exact, and its monoidal unit comparison identifies the stalks of the finite free constant sheaves with Λⁿ and Λᵐ. It therefore identifies the stalk of the sheaf dual with the kernel of the same transposed matrix on modules, namely Hom_Λ(M, Λ). Transport along M ≅ F_s yields the asserted module isomorphism. This uses finite presentation, not projectivity, and does not assert that stalks commute with internal Hom for arbitrary sheaves.
